finding.shortLabel: Candidate A eliminated: continuous Buckinghamshire/Northamptonshire residence, 1603-1653

sources.locator: The National Archives, Kew, E 115/180/113 — certificate of residence, John Gurney, Aylesbury half-hundred to Northamptonshire, 1641; not examined at image level

finding.statement: Candidate A's own chain -- the 1603 Stewkley baptism, the 1628 Bierton marriage to Alice Oliffe, the 1638-1653 Aylesbury family group, a 1641 government certificate of residence recording his move into Northamptonshire, and a 1650 Walgrave, Northamptonshire tenancy -- places one continuously documented Englishman in Buckinghamshire and Northamptonshire across exactly the years the Massachusetts John Gurney was building a life at Weymouth and Braintree, dying there in 1662/3. The 1661 Edlesborough John Gurney x Mary Kidgell marriage reinforces the same conclusion from a second angle: either it is Candidate A himself, eliminating him outright on his own English marriage seven weeks after the Braintree John buried his own first wife Mary and remarried, or it is a distinct Bucks household that simply accounts for one more English 'John + Mary' who is not the emigrant. The wider Bucks household map shows the county was in no way short of Gurneys named John, so the surname match carries little weight on its own. Candidate A is eliminated as the colonial emigrant.

finding.shortLabel: At least five distinct Buckinghamshire John Gurney households, 1621-1664

sources.locator: East Claydon, Chesham, Wing, and Cublington baptism entries
East Claydon burial 17 Apr 1654 (PR51/1/1); Chesham burials Jul 1672 and 11 Jun 1678 (D/A/T/42); Edward Gurny's son buried 2 Feb 1665 (B24)
Household map cross-reference to the marriage index
Luke Gurney's four Aylesbury children, 1621-1635; Edward Gurny's daughter baptized 1666

finding.statement: A walk of the Findmypast Buckinghamshire marriage, burial, and baptism indexes finds at least five distinct seventeenth-century John Gurney households beyond Candidate A's own: John Gurney + Elizabeth at East Claydon (children Elinor 1632, Samuel 1636; burial 17 Apr 1654); John Gurney + Elizabeth at Chesham (children Andtr, Martha; burials Jul 1672 and 11 Jun 1678); John Gurney + Anne at Wing (children James 1650, Elizabeth 1652); John Gurney + Mary at Cublington (son Isaac, baptized 1664, after the colonial John's own 1662/3 death); and a Luke Gurney household at Aylesbury (four children 1621-1635, not a John Gurney line). A seventh Aylesbury head of household, Edward Gurny, is separately documented (a son buried 1665, a daughter baptized 1666).
